# Apple Application Inventory Projection

REA can project one or more authenticated `inventory_artifact` Evidence records
for the same IPA, macOS `.app` directory, ZIP, or DMG into an Apple application
inventory. The projection is execution-free: it reports exact paths, content
hashes, detected formats, bundle anatomy, runtime-family hints, and path-based
bridge hypotheses. It does not parse plist or CMS semantics or claim observed
runtime calls.

Framework hints match complete path segments such as `React.framework`,
`ReactNative.framework`, `hermes.framework`, `Flutter.framework`, and
`UnityFramework.framework`. Substrings in `Preact.framework`,
`Community.framework`, or `MyApp.framework` do not identify those families.
A generic `App.framework` also does not identify Flutter by itself. Runtime
families remain inventory-derived hints, not observed loading. Generic framework
and dylib paths do not establish Swift or Objective-C; this projection does not
decode language metadata. A bridge basis is inferred from the native path and
repeated for each paired script, rather than proving a particular binding.

```sh
rea project-apple-application-graph '{"inventory_evidence":[<inventory_artifact Evidence>]}'
```

```json
{
  "name": "project_apple_application_graph",
  "arguments": {
    "inventory_evidence": ["<inventory_artifact Evidence>"]
  }
}
```

The result includes every component in each inventory category. Bridge
hypotheses are the path-based JavaScript/native pairs within each application
root. To keep their Cartesian expansion bounded, the projection limits the
serialized candidate array to 2 MiB. It computes the pair count and
exact UTF-8 JSON size before creating candidate objects, then retains a
deterministic prefix when the byte budget is exceeded. The result's
`bridge_candidate_coverage` reports total, emitted, and omitted pair counts;
overall coverage becomes `partial` and a limitation explains the omission.
Duplicate inventory pages are merged by artifact identity and occurrence path;
their Evidence IDs remain attached as source Evidence.

Content nodes identify bytes by SHA-256 and report only content-derived formats.
Each occurrence reports its own `artifact_kind`, `artifact_format`, and executable
permission. Identical bytes can therefore appear as a script, resource, or native
addon at different paths without overwriting another occurrence's role. Package
formats such as APK and IPA belong to the occurrence; their ZIP bytes share a
content format. Graph and directory identities use locale-independent Unicode
ordering.

For IPA inventories, archive components outside every application root remain
in the component lists. Their JavaScript and native candidates are grouped with
other unrooted components, preserving the inventory projection's path pairing
semantics without attributing them to an application bundle.

Coverage is `complete-within-inventory` when the supplied pages reconstruct the
complete authenticated inventory, and `partial` otherwise. A partial result
states that absence is unknown. Component arrays remain complete when candidate
hypotheses are omitted; component arrays still include every component from
the supplied inventory pages, and overall coverage is `partial` in that case.

Inventoried files whose bytes were not read, such as encrypted archive members,
are listed in `unavailable_components` with their original path, format,
encryption flag, limitations, and null content identity. The same application-root
and AppleDouble attribution rules apply. These files make overall coverage
`partial`; component absence is unknown even when `inventory_complete` is true.
Directories have no file bytes and symlinks remain in `symlinks`, so neither is
an unavailable file component. The additive field participates in `projection_id`,
including when empty, so Apple projection identifiers change.

## Application roots

| Inventory root                         | Application root                                    |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| IPA                                    | Each `Payload/<Name>.app`                           |
| `.app` directory                       | `.`, the inventoried bundle itself                  |
| Directory, ZIP, or DMG containing apps | Each outermost `<Name>.app` followed by `Contents/` |

File and slice occurrences supply component endpoints. Directory tree identities
remain in source inventory and bundle anatomy, and links remain in `symlinks`.

Root and layout discovery use known directories and ancestors implied by deeper
inventory paths. A leaf file or symlink named `*.app`, `Contents`, or `Versions`
does not establish that directory. Directory and authenticated-file identity are
selected before applying anatomy case preferences, so a file cannot shadow a
folded directory name or a directory shadow a metadata/signature file.

ZIP archives made with `ditto -c -k --keepParent` report `<Name>.app`. A DMG
reports `<image>.dmg/<Volume>/<Name>.app`; DMG child inventory needs the native
macOS mounting adapter. When a DMG has only its root identity, the projection is
`partial` and says that bundle absence is unknown. Other inventory formats, such
as APK or ASAR, are rejected as input errors.

An inventoried directory whose name ends in `.app` is its own root even when its
inventory is partial or lacks `Contents/`. For directory, ZIP, and DMG
inventories, components outside every application root are not attributed to
the application. This covers installers, disk-image extras, and AppleDouble
sidecars, which therefore stay out of runtime families and bridge candidates. A
limitation reports how many inventoried entries were left out. IPA projection
still lists every archive component, including `SwiftSupport/`.

`platforms` lists `macos` for application roots with `Contents/`. It lists `ios`
for shallow application roots that have an `Info.plist`. An application root
with neither, such as an empty inventory, has no platform.

## macOS bundle anatomy

`bundles` lists each application root and every nested bundle under it. Each
bundle reports its `parent_path`, `layout`, `info_plist_path`,
`executable_candidates`, and `signing_paths`.

| Layout                | Meaning         | Content directory                             |
| --------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `macos-deep`          | Has `Contents/` | `Contents/`, executables in `Contents/MacOS/` |
| `versioned-framework` | Has `Versions/` | Each real `Versions/<version>/`               |
| `shallow`             | Neither         | The bundle directory itself                   |

Roles are path conventions (`role_basis: "path-convention"`):

| Role                 | Path                                                            |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app-extension`      | `*.appex`                                                       |
| `xpc-service`        | `*.xpc`, including XPC services inside frameworks               |
| `framework`          | `*.framework`                                                   |
| `system-extension`   | `*.systemextension`                                             |
| `driver-extension`   | `*.dext`                                                        |
| `plug-in`            | `PlugIns/*.bundle`, `*.plugin`, `*.qlgenerator`, `*.mdimporter` |
| `resource-bundle`    | `Resources/*.bundle`, such as SwiftPM resource bundles          |
| `bundle`             | Any other `*.bundle`                                            |
| `login-item`         | `Contents/Library/LoginItems/*.app`                             |
| `helper-application` | `Contents/Helpers/*.app`                                        |
| `nested-application` | Any other nested `*.app`                                        |

The components also list:

- `privileged_helpers`: files directly in `Contents/Library/LaunchServices/`,
  where SMJobBless helpers live;
- `launchd_plists`: `.plist` files directly in `Contents/Library/LaunchAgents/`
  (`domain: "agent"`) or `Contents/Library/LaunchDaemons/` (`domain: "daemon"`),
  as used by SMAppService;
- `helpers`: files directly in `Contents/Helpers/`.

Symlinks are reported by path in `symlinks`. Their targets are not inventoried,
so a versioned framework is described through its real `Versions/<version>/`
directories rather than `Versions/Current`. A framework's `info_plist_path` is
`null`, with a limitation explaining why, when it has more than one real
`Versions/<version>/` directory (even if only one of them holds a plist,
because `Versions/Current` decides which one applies) or when its single
version directory has no `Resources/Info.plist`.

AppleDouble sidecar files (`._*` and `__MACOSX/`) are inventory facts, but they
describe neighbouring files. They are excluded from roots, bundle roles, and the
anatomy components.

The projection does not read plists. Use `inspect_plist` on a bundle's
`info_plist_path` or a launchd plist to read `CFBundleExecutable`, identifiers,
`SMPrivilegedExecutables`, `BundleProgram`, URL schemes, and usage descriptions.
Use `inspect_signature` on an executable candidate for code-signing claims.

## Dylib load resolution

`trace_dylib_resolution` answers which file each Mach-O dylib load reaches. It
runs on the active Mach-O, or on every executable in the active `.app`. Each
executable in a bundle (the main app, XPC services, app extensions, login items,
privileged helpers, and helper tools) is a separate process root with its own
`@executable_path`.

```sh
rea trace-dylib-resolution MyApp.app --json
rea trace-dylib-resolution MyApp.app --root Contents/MacOS/MyApp --architecture arm64 --json
```

```json
{
  "name": "trace_dylib_resolution",
  "arguments": { "roots": ["Contents/MacOS/MyApp"], "architecture": "arm64" }
}
```

Load commands are parsed in TypeScript from Mach-O and FAT headers, including
the `dylib_use_command` encoding newer linkers emit for flags such as delayed
initialization, and `LC_LAZY_LOAD_DYLIB_INFO` (`0x3a`). That command stores its
install name in a linkedit payload rather than in the load command itself.
Its flag and chain-start image offsets must lie in the slice VM range, which
is dyld's one-page floor extended by every segment except `__LINKEDIT`,
measured from the `__TEXT` vmaddr. Payload strings must start after the 24-byte
header. The load-path NUL must occur before the payload's final byte, matching
dyld's scan. Distinct payload bytes and payload-range lookups stay within the 16 MiB
limit, and a file range already read is reused. String scanning and UTF-8
checks count every reference, including repeats and overlaps, and stop at that
same aggregate. A slice retains at most 1024 of these commands; further copies are
unsupported instead of becoming one traced edge each. Symbol references,
including repeats, stop at 65536 per slice. A larger table is unsupported
instead of caching one string per offset.
Nothing is executed and no Apple tool is required, so the tool also works off
macOS.

Resolution follows dyld:

- `@executable_path` is the directory of the process root's executable. It is
  undetermined when the root is a library.
- `@loader_path` is the directory of the image that holds the load command, or
  of the image that owns the `LC_RPATH` entry being expanded.
- `@rpath` tries each `LC_RPATH` of the loading image first, then those of the
  image that loaded it, up to the process root.
- Dependencies load dependents-first in load-command order, and each image
  loads once per process. A later @rpath request whose install name matches an
  already loaded image reuses it.
- Symlinks such as `Versions/Current` are followed inside the analyzed root.
  An escape through `..` or an absolute link is `escapes-target`.

Each edge lists every candidate path tried, with its outcome: `resolved`,
`absent`, `not-mach-o`, `malformed`, `unsupported` (recognized Mach-O outside
parser coverage, such as big-endian images), `architecture-missing`,
`not-loadable`, `platform-mismatch`, `outside-target`, `escapes-target`, or
`undetermined`. `not-loadable` means a
matching-architecture Mach-O image was found but it is not a dylib and cannot
satisfy a dylib dependency. `platform-mismatch` means a matching-architecture
dylib was found but its observed platform is incompatible with the process.
These outcomes reject that candidate; dyld search may continue and resolve a
later candidate. Candidate outcomes describe individual search paths, while
`resolution.status` describes the final edge. For each selected process-root
slice, candidate slices are matched by CPU type and dyld's subtype preference
order, independently of FAT table order. An ARMv7s root slice prefers ARMv7s,
then ARMv7; other known ARM32 subtypes use their compatibility rows from
[Apple's dyld source](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/dyld/blob/dyld-852.2/src/dyld2.cpp#L2811-L3105).
An `x86_64h` process also loads generic `x86_64`. Unknown ARM32 subtype policy
remains undetermined when ARM32 candidate slices exist. This is a static model
keyed to the selected root slice; it does not observe the target device's host
CPU or prove which slice the device will execute. The edge's `resolution` is
one of:

| Status         | Meaning                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `resolved`     | An image inside the analyzed root loads, and no earlier candidate was undeterminable.                                                                          |
| `conditional`  | An in-root image may load, but an earlier outside candidate, unmodeled environment input, or unknown platform compatibility can change which image dyld loads. |
| `unresolved`   | Every candidate is definitively absent or unusable inside the root.                                                                                            |
| `undetermined` | No candidate resolves inside the root, and some candidate lies outside it or depends on the environment.                                                       |

A `conditional` image is still traced, because it is an in-root candidate
that may load. Every edge below it has `loader_conditional: true`, and a
request that reuses it by install name is `conditional` too. An in-root dylib
with no platform load command remains unknown unless the root is an executable
with observed macOS platform and the candidate’s CPU type is x86_64, i386, or arm64. In that macOS context,
[Apple's dyld](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/dyld/blob/fd8d0c4d52320ebf64db34f3cb280310d905c5ae/mach_o/UnsafeHeader.cpp#L1137-L1145) supplies an implicit macOS platform to legacy dylibs on those CPU
types. The candidate records `platform_basis: "macos-dyld-implicit"`; the
reported slice fields `platform: null` and `platforms: []` remain the parsed
facts. For other process contexts the platform remains unknown, coverage is
partial, and the candidate is not treated as incompatible. If a later known
candidate resolves, it remains the traced image with conditional resolution;
the trace does not claim the unknown candidate's dependency graph. Findings on
conditional edges say that they apply only if the conditional image loads.

Absolute install names that name a path beneath the analyzed root are checked
within that root, with symlinks and `..` resolved by the same bounded tree
resolver. Absolute paths outside the root, such as
`/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib`, are `outside-target`; on macOS 11 and later most
system libraries live in the dyld shared cache rather than on disk, so REA does
not check them against the host. Mach-O path strings are not converted from
`file:` URLs or looked up through unrelated host paths.

`findings` are derived, not observed:

- `required-load-unresolved`, `weak-load-unresolved`, and `lazy-load-unresolved`.
  `LC_LAZY_LOAD_DYLIB` and `LC_LAZY_LOAD_DYLIB_INFO` dependencies are resolved
  but not traversed, because dyld loads them on first use; an unresolved one is
  not a launch failure. `LC_LAZY_LOAD_DYLIB_INFO` has no compatibility version,
  so those fields are null. Its may-be-missing flag is reported as `weak`, and
  an unresolved dependency with that flag is not a first-use failure: dyld
  continues if the image is absent.
- `earlier-rpath-candidate-absent`: a compatible Mach-O placed at an earlier
  modeled search path could take precedence, subject to unmodeled search inputs
  and code-signing library validation. These findings do not establish which
  image dyld will load; use `inspect_signature` for signing metadata.
- `dyld-environment-present`: preserves observed `LC_DYLD_ENVIRONMENT` entries.
  Only an executable root supplies process settings; entries on library and
  other non-executable roots do not alter resolution or coverage. Applicable
  executable image-selection overrides are not modeled.

Empty dyld settings have different consumers. Modern dyld appends a slash and
image name to ordinary and fallback directory entries, so an empty entry can
search `/child.dylib` or `/Foo.framework/Foo`. REA retains uncertainty for those
unchecked paths; an empty fallback does not preempt an ordinary-search hit.
Empty versioned-directory lists do not scan a directory, and empty suffixes
only repeat the original candidate, so they do not add search uncertainty.
Reported command values are retained in all cases.

`verify:macos-bundle` checks the parser against `otool -l` for every traced
image. It also compares the predicted load order of two process roots with the
images dyld actually loads (`DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES`).

Setup preserves caller-owned Cordis expressions and replaces launcher fields
with literal values that doctor can verify. It refuses to edit an expression
that produces the entire REA config, or a group-targeted REA insertion. Use a
literal config and a root-level insertion as shown above.

For a global npm installation, the launcher is under
`$(npm root -g)/rea-agents/scripts/rea.mjs`. Restart Harness after setup; it
exposes tools as `mcp__rea__<tool_name>`. Run `rea setup --skill --dry-run`,
review the destination, then `rea setup --skill --yes` to install the workflow
in `~/.agents/skills` (`$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/skills` when configured); Harness
discovers that directory, and its native `skill` tool can load
`reverse-engineer-anything`.

REA's optional [native client verification](testing.md#end-to-end-integration-and-golden-evidence)
checks headless chat, skill loading, all tool input schemas and actual analysis
using the installed Harness and a local model fixture. This establishes the
Harness integration, with live DeepSeek API compatibility remaining unverified.
See the [Harness MCP guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84/packages/mcp/mcp-client/README.md)
for its native configuration contract.

## Other client settings

For OpenCode, setup writes the V1 `mcp.rea` entry, which OpenCode V1 and V2
both load. If the configuration already uses OpenCode V2's native
`mcp.servers` table, setup registers REA there instead and replaces any earlier
`mcp.rea` entry from REA. Setup honors `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` and
`OPENCODE_CONFIG`, preferring the later-loaded JSONC file when both JSON and
JSONC exist. The ordinary XDG global configuration still participates when a
custom directory is selected. Doctor checks the merged user registration; uninstall removes
REA-owned entries from every applicable user file so an older entry cannot
become active again. Malformed applicable files block setup before changes.

Grok Build loads `[mcp_servers.rea]` from `$GROK_HOME/config.toml`, or from
`~/.grok/config.toml` when `GROK_HOME` is unset or empty. Setup edits that server
table, `[mcp_servers.rea.env]`, and a root `disabled_mcp_servers` entry that
names `rea`. It sets `startup_timeout_sec = 30` and leaves every other name
in that list. The shared skill installed under `~/.agents/skills` is already
on Grok Build's skill path.

Grok Bot (`grok_bot`) is detected from `~/.grokbot`, or from `SAND_DATA_ROOT`
when that value is an absolute path. A relative or empty `SAND_DATA_ROOT`
stays on `~/.grokbot`. That directory is not the connector store. Grok Bot
keeps connectors in the signed-in account and runs them on its hosted
computer. It does not import `mcp.json` from the data directory, and it does
not attach a stdio server running on this machine. Setup does not call the
account connector API, does not write a registration file, and does not report
the data directory as aligned. Ask the Grok Bot chat to add a custom MCP
server named `rea` that runs on the Bot's computer:

```bash
npx -y rea-agents@<version> mcp
```

Do not put credentials in that command or its arguments. `rea doctor --client grok_bot`
reports this manual step. `rea uninstall` does not remove the account connector.

## Что такое REA

`morluto/rea` — это MCP-сервер для агентов: инвентаризация `.app`, разбор Mach-O/plist/подписей, дизассемблирование через Hopper/Ghidra/IDA, наблюдение за поведением процесса. Для нашей задачи подходит: поддерживает **OpenCode** как клиента, macOS-приложения, universal (FAT) бинари и Swift/ObjC.

Ставится не клоном репозитория, а официальным пакетом `rea-agents` (сейчас 6.7.0). Node у тебя 22.23.3 — требования пакета (`^22.19.0`) выполняются.

## Важное ограничение

Я сейчас в **Plan mode**, а установка меняет глобальный npm и `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. В этом режиме я не могу трогать файлы. Переключи агента в **build mode** — и я сразу выполню установку. Пока ничего не изменено.

## Что сделаю после переключения

```bash
# 1. Посмотреть план изменений без записи
npx rea-agents@6.7.0 setup --client opencode --dry-run --json

# 2. Установить и зарегистрировать MCP + skill (с бэкапом конфига)
npx rea-agents@6.7.0 setup --client opencode

# 3. Проверить готовность
npx rea-agents@6.7.0 doctor --client opencode --json
```

Setup добавит `mcp.rea` в `opencode.jsonc`, сохранит существующий `browseros-neo` и сделает `.rea.backup`. После этого нужен **перезапуск сессии OpenCode**, иначе MCP-инструменты не появятся.

Провайдер декомпилятора предлагаю **не ставить сразу**: базовые возможности REA (инвентарь бандла, plist, подпись, Mach-O, dylib-резолюция) работают без него. Если понадобится псевдокод — поставим Hopper (демо, ставится через REA с подтверждением) или бесплатный Ghidra + JDK 21. Для точечных вопросов по Swift-методам Hopper удобнее.

## Как будем использовать для ForkLift

Честно: **«портировать» нечего** — исходников нет, есть скомпилированный Swift/ObjC. REA ускорит не перенос, а **анализ и написание спецификации** для собственной реализации.

Предлагаю такой рабочий поток:

1. **R1. Инвентарь бандла** — фреймворки, helper, entitlements, storyboards/nib, локализации, ресурсы, подпись, URL-схемы. Это даёт карту компонентов.
2. **R2. Статическая структура** — Swift/ObjC-классы, методы, строковые кластеры, константы, ключевые протоколы (`SFTPDatasource`, `ActivityQueue`, `MultiRenameActivity` и т.п.). На выходе — архитектурная карта, не код.
3. **R3. Поведенческая спецификация** — гоняем ForkLift на тестовой папке: копирование, конфликты, undo, drag&drop, preview, очередь, горячие клавиши. Фиксируем наблюдаемое поведение и пишем тест-матрицу.
4. **R4. Приёмка** — наши интеграционные тесты воспроизводят ту же матрицу; расхождения чиним.

Результаты складываем в `docs/analysis/` и `docs/spec/` — **отдельно от кода**. Это clean-room: реализацию пишем по спецификации, а не копируем декомпилированный код, ассеты, иконки и название. REA в своём DISCLAIMER разрешает анализ только легально полученного ПО для интероперабельности; обход защиты и перенос проприетарного кода не используем.

## На что это повлияет в плане MVP

- Добавляется **2–3 дня** на R1–R3 перед M0.
- Декомпилятор — только по необходимости, для конкретных вопросов.
- Сам MVP остаётся тем же: локальный двухпанельный менеджер на Swift, ~2 недели.
- REA не заменяет проектирование и тесты; он даёт доказательную базу о том, как ведёт себя оригинал.

Переключи в build mode — запущу dry-run, покажу diff конфига, поставлю REA и начну с инвентаря `ForkLift.app`.

<skill_content name="reverse-engineer-anything">
# Skill: reverse-engineer-anything

# REA

Use REA when a claim depends on a shipped binary or package, decompilation,
passive application runtime evidence, or comparison with
behavior not established by available source. For ordinary analysis of a
complete source repository, use normal repository tools and do not run REA
readiness or provider commands.

## Connect only when needed

Installing this skill supplies instructions; it does not register the REA MCP
server, install analysis engines, or add tools to an already-running agent.

If REA tools are available and their registration is not known to be stale,
proceed directly to the target. Do not run diagnostics or setup before every
investigation. Use the connected server's actual tool list and input schemas;
a skill installed from repository main may describe capabilities absent from
an older npm release. Keep complete inline Evidence when that server does not
advertise retained references.

If tools are absent, a call is blocked by the client, or a required provider is
unavailable, read [connection and recovery](references/connection-and-recovery.md).
Diagnose the observed blocker, continue useful supported work, and resume the
original task after repair. Client approval, shell PATH, registration and engine
availability have different remedies; avoid repeating setup for all of them.

1. Diagnose without changing REA or client configuration. `npx` may download
   the package and write to npm's cache. For Codex, run
   `npx -y rea-agents@6.7.0 doctor --client codex --json`. Substitute the current
   supported client: `claude_code`, `claude_desktop`, `codex`, `cursor`,
   `gemini_cli`, `windsurf`, `devin`, `opencode`, `antigravity`, `copilot_cli`,
   `commandcode`, `vscode`, `grok_build`, `omp`, or `grok_bot`. `grok_bot` has no local
   file registration: doctor reports the Grok Bot chat step, and setup does not
   write `mcp.json`. If the client is unknown, use `doctor --json` and
   inspect its registration results before choosing a setup scope.
2. Distinguish the reason. Missing, malformed, or stale registration needs a
   scoped configuration repair. An aligned registration with no tools in the
   active session needs a restart/reconnection; doctor cannot prove that the
   current agent has connected. A missing provider affects only tasks requiring
   that provider: static JavaScript inspection needs neither Hopper nor Ghidra,
   and Android inspection has separate bring-your-own JADX/Java prerequisites.
3. For a configuration repair, prepare the read-only plan:
   `npx -y rea-agents@6.7.0 setup --client codex --dry-run --json`.
   Use the current client's ID, show its exact proposed paths, backups, and
   changes, and obtain approval before setup writes configuration or installs
   Hopper. Setup normally installs the matching bundled skill too; include that
   replacement in the reviewed plan. After approval, apply the same scope with
   `npx -y rea-agents@6.7.0 setup --client codex --yes`. Add `--install-hopper`
   only if that separate installation was needed and explicitly approved.
4. Restart/reconnect the affected agent. Verify that REA tools actually appear
   in the session, then resume the original investigation. If they remain
   absent, inspect the client's MCP launch error rather than repeating setup.

REA setup never installs or upgrades Node.js, npm, Homebrew, Java, Ghidra, IDA,
JADX, Kuna, Binwalk, or Unblob. Use existing prerequisites; do not install unrelated
software to repair
MCP registration. For an unsupported client, use manual stdio registration
with a version-pinned `rea-agents` package or continue through the CLI.

A concrete CLI fallback for an operator-supplied JavaScript tree or ASAR is:

```bash
npx -y rea-agents@6.7.0 analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json
```

No MCP registration or native engine is required. Read the returned Evidence,
graph, limitations, and unknowns with the same care as an MCP result; the CLI
returns the Evidence record directly. This fallback does not establish that
MCP is configured. Native CLI tasks still require their selected engine.
Prefer an existing `rea` CLI. When none is installed and REA package acquisition
is within the authorized scope, use `npx -y rea-agents@6.7.0` in its place.
Configuration repair starts with a read-only setup plan; show paths, backups and
skill replacement before applying authorized changes. Preserve existing approval
and target-execution boundaries. REA setup never installs or upgrades unrelated
software, including Node.js, npm, Homebrew, Java, Ghidra, IDA, JADX, Kuna, Binwalk or Unblob.

## Route the target first

Choose the first tool from the target the user supplied. Use `open_binary` for
active-target native or archive workflows; target-free tools take their own
explicit path or endpoint and do not need it.

- ASAR or extracted JavaScript/Electron tree:
  `analyze_javascript_application`.
- Archive/package member inventory (ZIP/APK/IPA/MSIX/AppX or DMG):
  `open_binary` with the supplied local path; use `inspect_artifact` when its
  graph and findings help answer the question.
- Android APK code, classes, methods, or incoming references:
  `inspect_android_package`, then focused Android tools when advertised.
  Archive member inventory still uses the archive route above.
- Managed PE/CLI assembly: `inspect_managed_artifact`.
- Firmware image: `inspect_firmware_regions` when advertised. Use
  `extract_firmware` when extraction is requested, with a caller-selected new
  absolute output directory. These tools use caller-supplied Binwalk/Unblob on
  Linux; see the [firmware guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/firmware-analysis.md).
- .NET NativeAOT PE/ELF: native Ghidra analysis. Native code can yield pseudocode;
  consult the NativeAOT workflow in `references/native-and-artifacts.md` for
  optional metadata recovery and its supported host/layout boundary.
- User-owned browser page already open: `list_browser_targets`.
- Browser action the agent must perform (click, type, navigate):
  `capture_browser_scenario` with declared actions. See
  [runtime observation](references/runtime-observation.md) for connect/launch
  and the focused follow-up browser tools.
- Fiddler Everywhere traffic or a native `.saz` capture: read the
  [Fiddler workflow](references/runtime-observation.md#fiddler-everywhere-traffic-debugging).
  Inspect saved SAZ with `inspect_web_network_capture` and `format: "saz"`;
  connect Everywhere's separate MCP server for live traffic.
- Retained HAR/SAZ/native mitmproxy/aioquic qlog capture: `inspect_web_network_capture`. Select
  original record ordinals when useful; inspect producer fields and byte/number
  sidecars without fetching recorded URLs or claiming live attribution. See
  [historical captures](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/web-network-captures.md) for the exact upstream
  profile and credential exclusions. Qlog support starts with aioquic 1.5.0
  JSON 0.3; stream coverage and endpoint loss declarations do not recover bodies
  or establish network loss. Prefer detail summary, then kind qlog trace/stream
  pages; select one trace, stream ID and direction for contribution/range pages.
  Facts retain all-recorded-events-before-selection scope. Other qlog layouts
  and PCAP correlation are unsupported.
- User-owned Electron runtime already open: `list_electron_targets`. Before an electron-main Inspector attempt, check packaged fuses with `inspect_electron_fuses`; disabled `EnableNodeCliInspectArguments` means the app ignores `--inspect`.
- Packet-field discovery: `inspect_packet_fields` searches installed protocols
  and field names/types before choosing fields for `inspect_packet_capture`.
  Query/page the relevant records; registrations do not establish observed traffic.
- Recorded packet captures: `inspect_packet_capture` with selected TShark fields,
  display filters and decode-as rules. Requires Linux, util-linux prlimit and `REA_TSHARK_COMMAND`; see
  [capture guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/packet-captures.md).
  Packet limits count input packets before filtering. Output defaults to 50 matching
  frames; use `match_offset` / `match_limit` for later pages, or explicit null
  limit for complete matching output. Preserve the source digest across pages.
  This does not perform live capture.
  For address/DNS/SNI/protocol summaries use `inspect_pcap_capture` with MCP
  detail summary, then retained kind pcap pages. Requires Wireshark 4.x tshark
  and capinfos, with Linux prlimit or Windows Job Objects; see
  [packet summaries](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/pcap-analysis.md).
  Select an exact DNS question for address pages; page exhaustion does not prove
  network completeness. This reads recordings and does not acquire traffic.
- Decoder discovery: `inspect_signal_decoders` searches installed decoder IDs
  or selected decoder help, including channels and options. Query and page the
  relevant details before choosing settings; this does not scan hardware.
- Recorded logic/signal traces: `decode_signal_recording` with explicit decoder,
  channel and protocol settings. On Linux with util-linux prlimit, supply sigrok-cli 0.7.2 through
  `REA_SIGROK_COMMAND`; see [recording guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/signal-recordings.md).
  Output defaults to 50 literal lines; select annotation classes and page with
  `line_offset` / `line_limit`, or explicit null for all remaining output.
  Window counts are display lines, not annotations or samples. Preserve source digests across pages.
  This reads existing files; it does not acquire hardware signals.
- Explicit local WebAssembly artifact: `inspect_wasm_artifact`. Supply WABT 1.0.42
  through `REA_WABT_BIN_DIRECTORY`; retain exact byte/tool identity and decoded WAT.
  Select JavaScript glue and candidate paths explicitly and preserve URL/path
  ambiguity. No implicit fetch or target execution; WAT is not original source.
  See the [WASM guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/wasm-artifacts.md).
- Explicit local EVM bytecode carrier: `inspect_evm_interface` with caller-selected
  `raw` or `hex` encoding. Preserve carrier/decoded digests and treat selectors,
  argument strings and mutability as inferred candidates; this performs no chain
  lookup or target execution. For the complete inferred interface without hex or
  duplicate stdout, discover support and select `detail: "summary"`; complete
  Evidence stays retained under its original identity. Use the returned
  `parent_evidence_id` for exact function or `bytecode_hex`/stdout/stderr pages.
  Candidate coverage does not establish interface completeness. See the
  [EVM bytecode guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/evm-bytecode.md).
- Embedded Go compiler, module or build-setting metadata: `inspect_go_binary`
  with the explicit local file. This built-in target-free inspection requires no
  Go installation or disassembler. Preserve raw module bytes and source ranges;
  absent metadata does not prove a binary is not Go, and unparsed text records
  remain explicit. See the
  [Go binary guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/go-binaries.md).
- Embedded cargo-auditable Rust dependency metadata: `inspect_rust_binary`
  with the explicit local ELF, PE, or thin Mach-O file. This built-in
  target-free inspection requires no Rust installation or disassembler. Preserve
  package order, dependency indices, and the section file range. A missing
  `.dep-v0` section is null metadata, not proof the binary has no dependencies.
  A rustc commit hash is an inference from a read-only `/rustc/<40-hex>/` path.
  See the
  [Rust binary guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/rust-binaries.md).

- Explicit local SQLite database snapshot: `inspect_sqlite_database`. Inspect
  with Node.js 24.x >=24.15 or 26+ providing native SQLite limits. Read schema
  first (compact inventory by default), or select an exact ordinary table
  and `columns` when rows are needed. Defaults are selected-table schema and
  20 rows; request `schema_scope: "database"` for the complete stored schema. Preserve both database and existing sibling WAL identity; row samples
  report truncation and have unspecified order. Use a quiescent snapshot rather
  than assuming a live database/WAL pair was copied atomically. See the
  [SQLite guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/sqlite-databases.md).
- Explicit Linux ELF file for offline layout, symbols, relocations or static
  mitigation evidence: `inspect_binary_layout`. This target-free operation uses
  caller-supplied pwntools without opening a disassembler database. Preserve its
  raw locations and inference/coverage limits; see the
  [offline binary guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/binary-diagnostics.md).
- Supplied Linux x86-64 ELF core: `inspect_recorded_crash`. Read every recorded
  thread, raw note and source-bound register without opening a live target.
  Historical PIDs do not select live processes. Request `include_debugger_context`
  only when core-only mapping candidates help; see the
  [recorded crash guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/recorded-crashes.md).
- PE resource type/name/language trees and static icon group references:
  `inspect_pe_resources` with an explicit path. This portable operation requires
  no active target or engine; opaque payloads retain file ranges and SHA-256.
- Native executable, library, or analysis database: `open_binary`, then
  use focused analysis tools directly; call `binary_overview` when metadata or
  inventory context is useful and available from the selected provider.

For an existing IDA MCP configuration, use `open_binary` with the original
input binary and `provider_id: "ida"`; do not pass an `.idb` or `.i64` database.
The legacy attached profile binds the already-open GUI input by SHA-256 and
leaves its database open. The modern headless profile creates and closes an
owned private database without saving. Installation and registration reuse
[mrexodia/ida-pro-mcp](https://github.com/mrexodia/ida-pro-mcp); see the
[IDA provider guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/ida-provider.md).
Proceed directly to `analyze_function`, pseudocode, or function/string searches
after opening; IDA does not supply `binary_overview`. Consult session availability
when composing broader workflows. Modern direct callers and unsupported dossier
facets remain unknown; live IDA results are not replayed from snapshots.

With `REA_KUNA_COMMAND` configured, `provider_id: "kuna"` answers procedure
lists, lookups, pseudocode, assembly and `analyze_function` from Kuna's cached
whole-program export. Callers/callees use a separate body-free graph shared by
the session; `xrefs` returns exact-address incoming sites and filters forwarding
aliases. These queries and inventory lookups do not trigger a C export. Indirect
targets remain unknown and can make relationship coverage partial. Reference
caches expire on close; a fresh CLI process repeats the native reference walk.
Typed references, CFG, raw-memory tools and annotations remain unsupported. A cold first
answer can come from a single-function run (its limitations say so); assembly
waits for the export. For pseudocode and assembly, `raw_result.source` names the
cached `.c`/`.asm` file and byte span, which you may search directly instead of
calling per function. See the
[Kuna provider guide](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/kuna-provider.md).

If the user says only "my app" without a name, path, or target already selected
for this task, ask which app before searching for artifacts. Paths in unrelated
saved reports and nearby test fixtures do not select the user's target. Resolve
an actual human-readable app name to one clear installed artifact when possible;
ask when matches are ambiguous. Never choose an example app on the user's behalf.

In a target-free session, use `open_binary` to bind any archive/package or
native target whose analysis tool operates on the active target. Do not call an
unadvertised tool; inspect `binary_session` with `{}` and its
`result.tool_availability` for availability reasons and remediation. Expand each
group's `names` into entries, inheriting the inventory-level client requirements
unless the group overrides them. In its closed effect and annotation vocabularies,
listed flags are true and omitted known flags are false. The grouped name union
is the complete tool inventory; use `tools/list` for canonical tool schemas.
Provider candidate facts describe possible providers, while top-level session
capabilities describe the current route and `analysis_provider_binding` names the
selected provider. Do not treat those scopes as interchangeable.

## Work summary-first

Start with the default result and use its inline Evidence and graph context.
For a JavaScript application or ELF layout whose size is unknown or large,
call `analyze_javascript_application` or `inspect_binary_layout` with
`"detail": "summary"`, then inspect the retained `parent_evidence_id` with
`inspect_analysis_view`.
Page module identities and select the returned `node_id` before requesting an
item; a single file path can represent several graph roles. Do not repeat an
identical analysis or rejected call without a changed input or resolved blocker.
Recheck session state when a lifecycle change makes that status useful.
Make a focused follow-up only when the
returned result leaves a specific question unanswered.

If MCP reports `resource_constraint` with `details.resource: "transport"`, call
`inspect_analysis_view` with its reported same-session Evidence reference for a
summary, one section/module, or a stable page. Use `trace_application_feature`
once a seed is known, or call `export_evidence_bundle` to write the complete
session to a selected path. The analysis remains complete in the ledger; avoid
repeating it merely to request the same oversized response. Complete CLI JSON
output also streams without a single MCP frame.

When the retained parent ID is unknown, use `get_evidence_bundle` with
`detail: "summary"` and exact filters for operation, target SHA-256,
analysis-profile digest or canonical procedure address. Select its returned
Evidence ID for the next view instead of requesting the complete bundle.
`retention: "complete-record"` means the whole record is stored; native
value-flow truncation and unknown metadata remain separate. For an exported
portable bundle, use `rea inspect-evidence-bundle` with JSON containing `path`,
`detail: "summary"` and the same `filters`. Reading that file still requires
validating its full contents within the local memory budget.

A client can also truncate a successful tool result without a REA transport
error. Treat that preview as incomplete; use the retained parent ID for smaller
views or export when the full record is needed. Do not parse the preview as
canonical JSON or repeat the producer. For JavaScript, read the
[module-view and trace recipes](references/javascript-applications.md) before
drilling into a large graph; a broad bidirectional trace can expand unrelated
containment relationships even after summary analysis.

Every conclusion must distinguish observations, inferences, and unknowns. Cite
Evidence IDs, preserve limitations and incomplete coverage, and never imply
that static analysis observed execution. Runtime requests execute the declared
target and lifecycle; do not broaden the target or action beyond those fields.

Within the user's requested investigation, call available analysis tools
directly. REA does not require permission grants or per-call approval flags.
The agent client can independently require approval. Follow the declared request
scope and the host's actual access requirements; use the recovery guide for an
observed client-policy rejection.

## Plan broader investigations

For requests that span multiple features or subsystems, use a staged workflow:

1. Turn the request into a checklist of questions and the evidence each answer
   needs. Resolve target identity and constraints from the conversation and
   workspace before asking for information again.
2. Inspect the current REA session, artifact identity, saved analysis database,
   bookmarks, and prior evidence. Reuse matching state; do not open duplicate
   sessions or repeat identical analysis.
3. Start with the smallest useful overview or inventory. Follow each question
   from its entry point through relevant data and state changes to its result.
   Batch related operations around a specific hypothesis, then expand only when
   the returned evidence leaves a concrete gap.
4. Inspect relevant packaged resources and configuration alongside code when
   they affect the question. Use format-aware inventory and parsers; do not
   infer behavior from filenames, strings, or layout alone.
5. Corroborate a conclusion with the evidence type it requires. Use runtime
   observation only when static evidence cannot answer the question and the
   required host runtime and OS access are available. For JavaScript behavior,
   run probes against the actual app through the available browser, Electron,
   or process capture workflow.
6. Decompose work into independent questions. When parallel workers are
   available and the questions do not depend on one another, assign distinct
   scopes, point workers to existing evidence, and ask them to return sources,
   conclusions, and unresolved gaps. Otherwise, work sequentially.
7. Keep a concise finding ledger linking each conclusion to Evidence IDs,
   confidence/evidence type, search boundary, and remaining unknowns. Update
   the shared index or investigation report so later passes can reuse results.

Before finishing, revisit the original checklist. Mark each question as
answered, partially answered, or unresolved based on its evidence; keep
bounded negative searches bounded, and do not describe a broad investigation
as complete while required questions remain open.

## Read only the relevant guide

- Native binaries, managed assemblies, archives, and extraction:
  [references/native-and-artifacts.md](references/native-and-artifacts.md)
- ASARs, extracted JavaScript, feature tracing, and version comparison:
  [references/javascript-applications.md](references/javascript-applications.md)
- Android APK declarations, classes, methods, and static references:
  [references/android-applications.md](references/android-applications.md)
- Browser/Electron observation (passive and scenario) and static/runtime
  reconciliation:
  [references/runtime-observation.md](references/runtime-observation.md)
- Evidence paging, comparisons, residual unknowns, and verification:
  [references/evidence-workflows.md](references/evidence-workflows.md)

## Finish the task

Explain findings in plain language and tie them to returned evidence. When the
user asks to build something, use normal coding tools and separate observed
behavior from design choices. Close an opened native session with
`close_binary` when the investigation is complete.

1: # Native, managed, and packaged artifacts
2: 
3: ## Go build metadata
4: 
5: Use `inspect_go_binary` for an explicit local ELF, PE or thin Mach-O when the
6: question concerns the embedded compiler version, module/dependency versions,
7: local replacements or build settings. No `open_binary`, Go installation or
8: target execution is required. The CLI equivalent is `inspect-go-binary PATH`.
9: Preserve artifact SHA-256, original file ranges, framed module bytes and every
10: unparsed module-text line. A missing record is an unknown, not proof of a
11: non-Go binary; observed metadata does not authenticate its claims. Function,
12: source and type recovery remain a separate native-analysis question.
13: 
14: ## Rust dependency metadata
15: 
16: Use `inspect_rust_binary` for an explicit local ELF, PE, or thin Mach-O when
17: the question concerns the cargo-auditable crate list embedded in `.dep-v0`
18: (Mach-O: `__DATA,.dep-v0`). No `open_binary`, Rust installation, or target
19: execution is required. The CLI equivalent is `inspect-rust-binary PATH`.
20: Preserve artifact SHA-256, package order, dependency indices, and the section
21: file range. A missing section is null metadata, not proof the binary has no
22: dependencies. An omitted package kind stays null. A rustc commit hash is
23: inferred from a read-only `/rustc/<40-hex>/` path and does not by itself
24: identify the compiler. See [Rust binaries](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/rust-binaries.md).
25: 
26: ## SQLite snapshots
27: 
28: Use `inspect_sqlite_database` with an explicit local database snapshot for its
29: schema and optional rows from one exact ordinary table. It requires Node.js
30: 24.x >=24.15 or 26+ with the native `DatabaseSync.limits` API. It also consumes the
31: existing sibling `-wal`; retain both original digests when citing its result.
32: Default output is a compact inventory; a selected table expands only its own
33: schema and samples 20 rows. Select `columns` to avoid irrelevant or large cells,
34: and request `schema_scope: "database"` only for complete schema details.
35: Choose `row_limit` when a finite sample is useful and keep truncation and
36: unspecified row order explicit. Virtual tables, shadow tables and views are
37: schema facts, not row-read targets. REA inspects private copies and leaves
38: the source files untouched; obtain a coherent quiescent database/WAL snapshot
39: before inspection. See [SQLite snapshots](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/sqlite-databases.md).
40: 
41: ## Recorded Linux crashes
42: 
43: Use `inspect_recorded_crash` with an explicit Linux x86-64 ELF core path to
44: inspect historical thread registers, signals, raw notes and original file
45: ranges. It is independent of the active disassembler target. Source-bound
46: register values and note bytes are observations; missing notes, signal-thread
47: association and current executable/library identity remain unknown. PIDs are
48: historical metadata and never authorize live attach or control.
49: 
50: The optional `include_debugger_context` facet adds mapping candidates through

52: establish current file identity; zero reported flags leave permissions unknown.
53: Requested unavailable context fails with setup guidance. See
54: [recorded crashes](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/recorded-crashes.md)
55: for exact upstream profiles, bounds and verification coverage.

9: returned inline. When complete `inspect_binary_layout` or
10: `analyze_javascript_application` Evidence is already retained, call
11: `inspect_analysis_view` for a summary, one section/symbol/module, or a stable
12: page instead of repeating the producer.
13: 
14: Completed `inspect_artifact` inventory also supports a summary and
15: `view: {kind: "inventory", collection: "occurrences", logical_paths: ["package.json", "main.js"]}`.
16: Omit `logical_paths` to page all available occurrences; `[]` selects none.
17: Other inventory collections are `nodes`, `edges` and
18: `integrity_contradictions`. Keep `source_complete` separate from page exhaustion:
19: a missing match in partial source Evidence does not establish absence. Use the
20: returned parent Evidence ID for subsequent views and export before closing the
21: session when the source must survive it.
22: When `tools/list` advertises `inspect_artifact.detail`, request `"summary"` to
23: retain its complete source and receive that view immediately. Without that
24: advertised choice, keep the existing complete call. CLI inspection returns
25: portable complete Evidence; save it before projecting a selected inline view.
26: 
27: Use `record_unknown` to track unresolved questions in the user's investigation
28: and name the authority or environment still required. Supply supporting and
29: contradicting evidence IDs. It updates the session registry directly.
30: Use `update_unknown` with the current revision; reread after a stale revision
31: instead of retrying blindly. Only qualifying observed evidence can verify a
32: resolution.
33: 
34: Use comparisons with complete, compatible page sets when claiming equivalence
35: or absence:
36: 
37: - `compare_artifacts` compares inventory pages by occurrence path, content,
38:   metadata, and graph relations.
39: - `compare_functions` compares explicit function Evidence, not fuzzy
40:   whole-binary matches.
41: - `compare_bundles` compares canonical bundle membership and unknown history.
42: - `find_changed_behavior` combines existing comparisons; static differences
43:   remain candidates, not causal proof.
44: - `build_call_path` needs explicit function dossiers from one artifact/provider;
45:   an incomplete frontier makes absence unknown.
46: - `correlate_static_and_runtime` uses explicit mappings; matching patterns are
47:   hypotheses, not causality.
48: - `verify_reconstruction` evaluates a finite typed specification. A pass covers
49:   only declared comparable claims, not global equivalence.
50: 
51: Process captures are opt-in behavioral evidence, not a security sandbox. V3
52: captures cannot be upgraded to V4; rerun the original scenario. Distinguish root
53: exit from descendant settlement and require freshness when the task needs it.
54: A timed-out target that must write a final report needs `finalization_ms`: REA
55: sends SIGTERM to the captured root, keeps observing, and sends SIGKILL once
56: only if the target has not exited by the end of the interval.
57: `exit.finalization.signals` lists each attempt with its delivery result; the
58: observed exit signal stays in `exit.signal`, `exit.code` is null for every
59: deadline exit, and the code of a finalizer that exited on its own is in
60: `exit.finalization.exit_code` (null on a signal exit or when no exit was
61: observed).
62: 
63: Use `inspect_analysis_view` with `view: {kind: "api-surface"}` on retained
64: `inspect_web_network_capture` HAR Evidence to group observed request lines by
65: method, origin and path template. Format matches are inferences, not handler
66: identity or schemas. Group pages cite parent record ordinals; consult record
67: coverage and exclusions before claiming completeness. No requests are replayed.
68: When the connected schema advertises `include_query_parameter_names`, select
69: it in the view for distinct observed names with original record ordinals. Query
70: values are omitted; the names establish neither required parameters nor a
71: complete server schema. Keep the original parent Evidence for exact URLs.

Inventory views page nodes, occurrences, edges or integrity contradictions; occurrence logical_paths matches exact recorded strings (omitted means all available, [] means none). source_complete distinguishes complete inventories from partial source records; page exhaustion does not prove absence in a partial source. WASM views use kind wasm and facet sections/imports/exports/candidates/glue/wat/headers/details/tool_profile; text facets use UTF-16 code units and source forms remain exact. Mach-O views use kind macho and facet entrypoints/architectures/build_metadata/load_commands/dependencies/imports/exports/segments/provenance; source_exhaustive false means unreturned rows may exist. Interface Builder views use kind interface-builder and collection documents/nodes/edges/coverage; nodes and edges accept an exact document relative_path. EVM summary returns all inferred interface candidates, carrier/decoded identities and explicit unknowns without hex or duplicate stdout. Exhausting candidate pages does not establish global interface completeness. Managed artifact summaries preserve complete identity/classification, metadata status, module/MVID, frameworks, coverage and limitations without unrelated inventories. Managed pages use kind managed and collection references/resources/attributes, retaining source coverage and build-local token scope; page exhaustion does not establish complete metadata. Managed member summaries keep identity, selection with unmatched names, coverage and per-collection counts; managed-members pages use collection types/exported_types/fields/methods/member_refs/call_edges/field_accesses/user_strings and carry the source selection and coverage. Android package summaries retain all declarations, engine identity and counts without decoded manifest text. ```json
{
  "command": "cat > /tmp/parse_menu.py <<'PY'\nimport json, base64, collections\nd=json.load(open('/tmp/forklift-ib.json'))\ng=d['data']['normalized_result']['graph']\nnodes={}\nfor n in g['nodes']:\n    if 'MainMenu.nib' not in n['id']: continue\n    nid=n['id'].split('object:')[-1].strip('[]\"') if 'object:' in n['id'] else None\n    if nid: nodes[nid]=n\ndef nv(n): return (n.get('attributes') or {}).get('nibValues') or {}\ndef objid(v):\n    return str(v.get('objectID')) if isinstance(v,dict) and 'objectID' in v else None\ndef string_for(ref):\n    oid=objid(ref)\n    if oid is None: return ''\n    n=nodes.get(oid)\n    if not n: return ''\n    v=nv(n)\n    if 'NSDev' in v: return v['NSDev']\n    if 'NS.bytes' in v:\n        b=v['NS.bytes']\n        if isinstance(b,dict) and '$nib_data_base64' in b:\n            try: return base64.b64decode(b['$nib_data_base64']).decode('utf-8','replace')\n            except: pass\n    return n.get('name') or ''\ndef maskstr(m):\n    if not isinstance(m,int): return ''\n    out=''\n    if m & (1<<20): out+='⌘'\n    if m & (1<<19): out+='⌥'\n    if m & (1<<18): out+='⌃'\n    if m & (1<<17): out+='⇧'\n    if m & (1<<16): out+='fn'\n    return out\n# actions by source object id\nactions=collections.defaultdict(list)\nfor n in g['nodes']:\n    if 'MainMenu.nib' not in n['id']: continue\n    a=n.get('attributes') or {}\n    if a.get('type')=='action' and a.get('source_id'):\n        actions[str(a['source_id'])].append(a.get('selector',''))\nmenus={}\nfor oid,n in nodes.items():\n    v=nv(n)\n    if v.get('NSClassName')=='NSMenu' or n.get('attributes',{}).get('class_name')=='NSMenu':\n        menus[oid]=string_for(v.get('NSTitle'))\nrows=[]\nfor oid,n in nodes.items():\n    a=n.get('attributes') or {}; v=nv(n)\n    if a.get('class_name')!='NSMenuItem': continue\n    title=string_for(v.get('NSTitle'))\n    key=v.get('NSKeyEquiv') or ''\n    mask=maskstr(v.get('NSKeyEquivModMask'))\n    menu=objid(v.get('NSMenu'))\n    sel=','.join(actions.get(oid,[]))\n    sep=v.get('NSIsSeparator')\n    if not title and not sep and not sel: continue\n    rows.append((menus.get(menu,'?'), title, mask, key, sel))\nrows.sort(key=lambda r:(r[0],r[1]))\nwith open('/tmp/forklift-menu.tsv','w') as f:\n    for r in rows: f.write('\\t'.join(str(x) for x in r)+'\\n')\nprint('menus:',len(menus),'items:',len(rows))\nfor r in rows[:80]: print('\\t'.join(str(x) for x in r))\nPY\npython3 /tmp/parse_menu.py"
}

Now, what does this mean for our clone:

1. **Adopt command protocol**: `BrowserCommand` enum + `Commands` protocol implemented by window controller; menu validation via `validateUserInterfaceItem`. This gives centralized behavior and keyboard shortcuts.
2. **View modes**: abstract `BrowserViewController` (BaseViewMode) with List/Column/Icon subclasses; share sorting/grouping/selection/drag logic. Our MVP can implement List + Icon; column later.
3. **Datasource abstraction**: even local files behind `FileProvider`; remote later. ForkLift's `LocalDatasource`, `ArchiveDatasource`, `SearchDatasource` show this pattern. We planned `FileProvider`; confirm.
4. **Activity queue**: each operation is an `Activity` object with title/info/logTitle/undoTitle/run; queue schedules, supports undo/redo. Our design should model `FileOperation` similarly with metadata for activity log and undo.
5. **File model**: `Fileinfo` (metadata, pasteboard, QL preview) + `Fileitem` (tree node with children, datasource). Separate value metadata from tree nodes; useful for large dirs.
6. **Persistence**: favorites are just a transformable dictionary in Core Data; we can use JSON/SwiftData; no need to over-model. Window/view settings via `ViewSettings` NSSecureCoding.
7. **Path bar & tabs**: `TabItemWrapper`, `PathBarModel`, `MouseEventView.TabCloseView`.
8. **Privileged helper**: 12 operations (copy/move/delete/create dir/size/owner/permissions/xattr/trash). We can defer; use `FileManager` and prompt for admin only later.
9. **Archives**: XADMaster third-party; local archive browsing via datasource. We'll use system `libarchive`/ZIPFoundation or integrate XADMaster (LGPL) later.
10. **Remote editing**: EditorViewController + UploadOperation/NSFilePresenter; later.
11. **Sync**: SyncEngine + SyncItem tree; later.
12. **Search**: SearchDatasource (likely Spotlight/NSMetadataQuery); later.
13. **Preview**: QLPreviewPanel integration in FileWindow (delegate/data source), QuickLookItem, plus InfoViewController.
14. **Menu map**: use as keybinding reference. Note some odd duplicates (Deselect All/Invert Selection both ⌘⌥A) because menu items use alternate key equivalents? Could be a decode artifact or localization; don't blindly copy.
15. **Column identifiers**: adopt name, size, kind, tags, modified, created, added, lastOpened, permissions, owner, group, comments, version, dimensions, duration, etc. MVP subset name/size/kind/modified; support more later.
16. **Window layout**: sidebar + two panes + toolbar 11 items + path bar + status bar; tabs per pane.
17. **Performance**: NSTableView/NSOutlineView with diffable data source; avoid reloadData; async metadata.

## Установка

- `rea-agents@6.7.0` зарегистрирован в OpenCode как MCP-сервер (`mcp.rea`), конфиг сохранён с бэкапом `opencode.jsonc.rea.backup`.
- Установлен skill `reverse-engineer-anything` (207 инструментов).
- `rea doctor --client opencode` → **healthy**. Провайдер декомпилятора не ставил — для текущего анализа он не понадобился.

## Что удалось выяснить без декомпилятора

**Поставка**
- ForkLift 4.7.7 (486), universal, 45 МБ, macOS 14.6+, hardened runtime, **без sandbox**, Developer ID, Sparkle, AppleScript, 13 локализаций.
- Внутри: Sparkle, XADMaster, UniversalDetector, привилегированный helper (12 XPC-операций) и sandboxed `AskPassTool`.

**Архитектура**
- 281 ObjC-видимый класс, 51 протокол, 1 689 ivar, 1 318 реализаций, 27 Swift-conformance.
- `FileWindow` — центральный хаб (178 методов); есть протокол `ForkLift.Commands` на **47 команд**.
- Режимы отображения: `BaseViewMode` (58 методов) + `ListView`, `ColumnView`, `IconViewController`.
- Источники: `Datasource` + Local / Archive / Search / FTP / SFTP / WebDAV / S3 / Backblaze / Dropbox / Google Drive / OneDrive / Rackspace.
- Операции: `Activity` + `ActivityQueue` с undo/redo и 20+ наследниками (copy, delete, rename, compress, extract, tags, permissions и т.д.).
- Модель файла разделена на `Fileinfo` (метаданные/pasteboard/QuickLook) и `Fileitem` (узел дерева).
- Избранное — Core Data с одной сущностью `Favorite` и transformable-словарём `data`.

**UI**
- Меню-бар: Apple, ForkLift, File, Edit, View, Go, Favorites, Commands, Purchase, Window, Help.
- Из storyboards извлечено 224 пункта меню с селекторами и сочетаниями.
- Колонки List view: name, size, tags, kind, modified, lastOpened, created, added, permissions, owner, group, comments, version, dimensions, duration и др.
- Окно: sidebar + две панели + toolbar (11 элементов) + path bar + status bar; подтверждено accessibility-деревом.

## Файлы в репозитории

- `docs/analysis/forklift-4.7.7.md` — полный отчёт с Evidence ID и границами анализа.
- `docs/analysis/data/forklift-classes.tsv` — 281 класс.
- `docs/analysis/data/key-class-selectors.txt` — селекторы ключевых классов + протоколы команд/helper.
- `docs/analysis/data/forklift-menu.tsv` — 224 пункта меню.
- `docs/analysis/data/forklift-table-columns.txt` — колонки.
- `docs/spec/mvp.md` — обновлённая спецификация MVP с учётом findings.
- `docs/README.md` — индекс и команды воспроизведения.

## Что это меняет в плане

Ключевые решения, которые теперь зафиксированы в спецификации:

1. **Command-паттерн** — один enum команд и один обработчик для меню, toolbar и клавиатуры.
2. **`FileProvider` с первого дня** — даже локальный доступ через протокол, чтобы удалёнка не ломала UI.
3. **`Activity`-модель** — операция как объект с прогрессом, логом и обратимостью; undo на уровне очереди.
4. **Разделение метаданных и дерева** — `FileItem` + `BrowserNode`.
5. **Избранное — простой Codable-формат**, без повторения Core Data-схемы.

## Ограничения и следующий шаг

Декомпилятор не установлен, поэтому точная логика конфликтов, отмены, `clonefile`, FSEvents и sync пока не доказана — это вынесено в открытые вопросы. Для MVP эти детали можно закрыть runtime-тестами; Hopper/Ghidra понадобится только если поведение не удастся установить чёрным ящиком.

Xcode всё ещё не установлен (`xcode-select` указывает на CommandLineTools). Для M0 по плану он нужен. Варианты:

1. Ты ставишь Xcode — я начинаю M0 (каркас, две панели, команды).
2. Пока делаю каркас на SPM без Xcode, а потом мигрирую на проект.
3. Сначала прогоняю runtime-сценарии ForkLift (конфликты, отмена, undo) и дополняю спецификацию.

class Ghidra < Formula
  desc "Multi-platform software reverse engineering framework"
  homepage "https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra"
  url "https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/archive/refs/tags/Ghidra_12.2_build.tar.gz"
  sha256 "ade4fd6e277a10c82db4e75ff5acaeedb3113ef0c7d126ea2c8b38c37128f3c3"
  license "Apache-2.0"

  livecheck do
    url :stable
    regex(/^Ghidra[._-]v?(\d+(?:\.\d+)+)(?:[._-]build)?$/i)
  end

  depends_on "gradle" => :build
  depends_on "python@3.15" => :build
  depends_on "openjdk@25"

  def install
    ENV["JAVA_HOME"] = Language::Java.java_home("25")
    inreplace "Ghidra/application.properties", "DEV", "PUBLIC" # Mark as a release
    system "gradle", "-I", "gradle/support/fetchDependencies.gradle"

    system "gradle", "buildNatives"
    system "gradle", "assembleAll"

    libexec.install (buildpath/"build/dist/ghidra_#{version}_PUBLIC").children
    (bin/"ghidraRun").write_env_script libexec/"ghidraRun",
                                       Language::Java.overridable_java_home_env("25")
    (bin/"pyghidraRun").write_env_script libexec/"support/pyghidraRun",
                                         Language::Java.overridable_java_home_env("25")

    # remove incompatible native binaries
    os = OS.mac? ? "mac" : "linux"
    arch = Hardware::CPU.arm? ? "arm_64" : "x86_64"
    (libexec/"GPL/DemanglerGnu/os").children
                                   .each { |dir| rm_r(dir) if dir.basename.to_s != "#{os}_#{arch}" }
    (libexec/"Ghidra/Features").glob("{Decompiler,FileFormats}/os/*")
                               .each { |dir| rm_r(dir) if dir.basename.to_s != "#{os}_#{arch}" }
  end

  test do
    (testpath/"analyzeHeadless").write_env_script libexec/"support/analyzeHeadless",
                                                  Language::Java.overridable_java_home_env("25")
    (testpath/"project").mkpath
    system "/bin/bash", testpath/"analyzeHeadless", testpath/"project",
                        "HomebrewTest", "-import", "/bin/bash", "-noanalysis"
    assert_path_exists testpath/"project/HomebrewTest.rep"
  end
end

/** Ghidra build whose bridge behavior this REA release verifies. */
export const SUPPORTED_GHIDRA_VERSION = "12.1.4";
/** Verified JDK major; admission uses the installation's declared bounds. */
export const SUPPORTED_GHIDRA_JAVA_MAJOR = 21;
const GHIDRA_RELEASE_PATTERN = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?([-+].*)?$/u;
/** Classify `application.version` against the verified release line. */
export const ghidraReleaseCompatibility = (raw) => {
    if (raw === null || raw === undefined)
        return { status: "unresolved", raw: null };
    const version = parseGhidraRelease(raw);
    if (version === undefined)
        return { status: "unresolved", raw };
    if (raw === SUPPORTED_GHIDRA_VERSION)
        return { status: "verified", version, raw };
    const verified = verifiedGhidraRelease();
    return version.major === verified.major && version.minor === verified.minor
        ? { status: "compatible", version, raw }
        : { status: "unsupported", version, raw };
};
/**
 * Limitation recorded when a session runs a compatible build other than the
 * verified release. The observed version stays on the provider identity.
 */
export const unverifiedGhidraBuildLimitation = (providerVersion) => {
    const compatibility = ghidraReleaseCompatibility(providerVersion);
    if (compatibility.status !== "compatible")
        return undefined;
    return `This session uses Ghidra ${providerVersion}. The bridge is verified against ${SUPPORTED_GHIDRA_VERSION}; other ${ghidraReleaseLine()} builds are accepted and the observed version is reported.`;
};
/** Release line accepted by this bridge, such as `12.1.x`. */
export const ghidraReleaseLine = () => {
    const verified = verifiedGhidraRelease();
    return `${String(verified.major)}.${String(verified.minor)}.x`;
};
/** Detail for the installation version check, including the accepted line. */
export const ghidraVersionDetail = (raw) => {
    const compatibility = ghidraReleaseCompatibility(raw);
    switch (compatibility.status) {
        case "unresolved":
            return compatibility.raw ?? "unknown";
        case "verified":
            return compatibility.raw;
        case "compatible":
            return `${compatibility.raw}; compatible ${ghidraReleaseLine()} release (verified build ${SUPPORTED_GHIDRA_VERSION})`;
        case "unsupported":
            return `${compatibility.raw}; accepted releases are ${ghidraReleaseLine()} (verified build ${SUPPORTED_GHIDRA_VERSION})`;
        default: {
            const unreachable = compatibility;
            return unreachable;
        }
    }
};
/** Whether this release line can run the packaged bridge. */
export const ghidraReleaseAccepted = (raw) => {
    const status = ghidraReleaseCompatibility(raw).status;
    return status === "verified" || status === "compatible";
};
const verifiedGhidraRelease = () => {
    const version = parseGhidraRelease(SUPPORTED_GHIDRA_VERSION);
    if (version === undefined)
        throw new TypeError(`SUPPORTED_GHIDRA_VERSION ${SUPPORTED_GHIDRA_VERSION} is not a Ghidra release`);
    return version;
};
const parseGhidraRelease = (raw) => {
    const match = GHIDRA_RELEASE_PATTERN.exec(raw);
    const major = integerGroup(match?.[1]);
    const minor = integerGroup(match?.[2]);
    if (match === null || major === undefined || minor === undefined)
        return undefined;
    const patch = match[3] === undefined ? 0 : integerGroup(match[3]);
    return patch === undefined
        ? undefined
        : { major, minor, patch, suffix: match[4] ?? "" };
};
/**
 * The version spelling Ghidra's `ApplicationVersion.toString` uses in its
 * settings directory: numeric components normalized, a zero patch and an
 * empty tag omitted. A build-metadata (`+`) suffix has no such spelling.
 */
export const ghidraConfigurationVersion = (raw) => {
    const version = parseGhidraRelease(raw);
    if (version === undefined || version.suffix.startsWith("+"))
        return undefined;
    const patch = version.patch === 0 ? "" : `.${String(version.patch)}`;
    const suffix = version.suffix === "-" ? "" : version.suffix;
    return `${String(version.major)}.${String(version.minor)}${patch}${suffix}`;
};
const integerGroup = (value) => {
    if (value === undefined)
        return undefined;
    const parsed = Number(value);
    return Number.isSafeInteger(parsed) ? parsed : undefined;
};

47: association and current executable/library identity remain unknown. PIDs are

61: without opening a disassembler target. When that complete record is already

72: or complete detail keeps the existing complete result.

74: reference for a summary or `view: {kind: "wasm", facet: "exports", offset: 0, limit: 32}`.
75: Facets also include sections, imports, candidates, glue, WAT, headers, details

77: The complete source remains retained after an oversized MCP reply. No target

    };
    const configuredEnvironment = await supportOutput("-envvars");
    options.onStderr("-envvars", configuredEnvironment.stderr);
    for (const line of configuredEnvironment.stdout.split(/\r?\n/u)) {
        if (line === "")
            continue;
        const separator = line.indexOf("=");
        const sourceKey = line.slice(0, separator);
        const key = options.platform === "win32" ? sourceKey.toUpperCase() : sourceKey;
        if (separator < 1 || !/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/u.test(key))
            throw new Error(`Invalid Ghidra LaunchSupport environment entry: ${line}`);
        if ((environment[key] ?? "") === "")
            environment[key] = line.slice(separator + 1);
    }
    const configuredMaxHeap = environment.GHIDRA_HEADLESS_MAXMEM || environment.GHIDRA_MAXMEM || "2G";
    // The merged environment becomes the analysis JVM's environment, and the
    // JVM applies these options variables automatically. An injected
    // -Dos.arch/-Dos.name there selects an unvalidated native directory without
    // appearing in vmArguments, so reject the effective values as well.
    for (const key of [
        "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS",
        "_JAVA_OPTIONS",
        "JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS",
    ]) {
        rejectJvmPlatformOverrides(jvmEnvironmentArguments(environment[key] ?? ""));
    }
    const configuredArguments = await supportOutput("-vmargs");
    options.onStderr("-vmargs", configuredArguments.stderr);
    const vmArguments = configuredArguments.stdout
        .split(/\r?\n/u)
        .filter((line) => line !== "");
    if (vmArguments.some((argument) => !argument.startsWith("-") || argument.includes("\0")))
        throw new Error("Invalid Ghidra LaunchSupport JVM argument");
    rejectJvmPlatformOverrides(vmArguments);
    return {
        command,
        environment,
        configuredMaxHeap,
        arguments: [
            ...vmArguments,
            ...(options.platform === "darwin" ? ["-Xdock:name=Ghidra-Headless"] : []),
            `-Xmx${configuredMaxHeap}`,
            "-XX:ParallelGCThreads=2",
            "-XX:CICompilerCount=2",
            "-Djava.awt.headless=true",
            ...isolatedProperties,
            "-showversion",
            "-cp",
            join(installRoot, "Ghidra", "Framework", "Utility", "lib", "Utility.jar"),
            "ghidra.Ghidra",
            "ghidra.app.util.headless.AnalyzeHeadless",
            ...options.arguments,
        ],
    };
};

\"LocalDatasource\", \"Datasource\",\n        \"FileWindow\", \"Fileinfo\", \"Fileitem\",\n        \"SyncEngine\", \"SyncItem\", \"SearchDatasource\",\n        \"FSEvent\", \"DeleteActivity\",      names.close();\n        println(\"TOTAL FUNCTIONS \" + fm.getFunctionCount());\n        println(\"SELECTED \" + selected.size());\n\n        PrintWriter out = new PrintWriter(outDir + @Override\n    public void run() throws Exception {\n        String targetFile = System.getenv(\"REA_TARGET_FILE\");\n        String outFile = System.getenv(\"REA_OUT\");\n        if (outFile == null (!ifc.openProgram(currentProgram)) {\n            println(\"OPEN FAILED \" + ifc.getLastMessage());\n            return;\n        }\n        PrintWriter out = new PrintWriter(outFile, \"UTF-8\");\n        int ok = 0, fail = 0, missing = 0;\n        try (BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(targetFile))) {\n            String line;\n            while ((line = br.readLine()) != null) {\n                line = line.trim();\n                if (line.isEmpty() || line.startsWith(\"#\")) {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                Function f = null;\n                if (line.startsWith(\"0x\")) {\n                    Address a = toAddr(line);\n                    f = fm.getFunctionAt(a);\n                    if (f == null) {\n                        f = fm.getFunctionAt(s.getAddress());\n                        if (f != null) {\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                if (f == null) {\n                    out.println(\"/* ===== MISSING \" + line + \" ===== */\");\n                    missing++;\n                    continue;\n                }\n                out.println(\"/* ===== \" + f.getEntryPoint() + \" \" + f.getName() + \" =====\");\n                try {\n                    DecompileResults res = ifc.decompileFunction(f, 180, res.getErrorMessage()));\n                        fail++;\n                    }\n                } catch (Exception e) {\n                    out.println(\"// ERROR \" + e);\n                    fail++;\n                }\n                out.println(\"*/\");\n                out.flush();\n            }\n        }\n        out.close();\n        ifc.dispose();\n        println(\"SELECTED ok=\"
